ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cue-Grounding Multiple-Choice Probe on MAFW and MER2024
PROPOSAL: Build a closed-form probe from 600 clips of MAFW and MER2024. Annotators list the audio and visual cues that explain the labelled emotion, and 3 distractor cues are attached to each clip: an irrelevant cue such as attire color, ambient noise, and a cue absent from the clip. Score Qwen2.5-Omni 7B and video-SALMONN 2 7B by option log-likelihood, so no external judge is needed. Report cue selection accuracy, the rate of picking irrelevant versus absent cues, and emotion accuracy conditional on a correct cue pick.
CONTROLS: Text-only run with the clip removed to estimate the text-prior rate; random-option floor; shuffled clip-cue pairings; annotator agreement on a 100 clip subset.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Models pick absent cues more often than irrelevant ones when the text-only run already favours them, and accuracy conditional on a correct cue pick exceeds unconditional accuracy. It fails if text-only accuracy sits near full-input accuracy, since the probe then measures priors only.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Free-Form Description Audit of Invented Cues on MAFW
PROPOSAL: Sample 300 MAFW clips and have Qwen2.5-Omni 7B write an emotion description for each under 8 decoding seeds. Extract cue claims with a fixed lexicon of audio and visual cue phrases and check the claims against clip-level cue tags from 2 annotators. Report the rate of claims absent from the clip and the rate tied to irrelevant cues, and how both change at decoding temperatures 0.3, 0.7 and 1.0. Compare the greedy description with the sampled ones to see whether sampling changes which cues get invented in the text. Clip-level tags are read from the dataset release.
CONTROLS: Lexicon applied to annotator reference captions; clips with audio muted; clips with frames blurred; scrambled-tag baseline pairing clips with tags from another clip.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Absent-cue claims rise with temperature and concentrate on cues that co-occur with the labelled emotion, such as tears with crying. It fails if the lexicon misses paraphrased cues, which would understate claim rates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Audio-Only versus Video-Only Ablation of Emotion Cue Use
PROPOSAL: Run Qwen2.5-Omni 3B on 400 CREMA-D and RAVDESS clips under 4 input conditions: full audiovisual, audio only, video only, and audio paired with video from a different emotion. Prompt for an emotion label plus a one-sentence cue explanation. Score label accuracy and, by keyword match against a cue list, the fraction of explanations that cite a modality that was removed or mismatched. A drop in accuracy alongside persistent citations of the missing modality would point to invention from text priors rather than perception.
CONTROLS: Majority-label baseline; text-only prompt naming only the spoken sentence; the same protocol on a second prompt wording.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Explanations keep citing the removed modality in a sizable share of audio-only and video-only clips, and mismatched clips expose label bias toward the text prior. It fails if accuracy barely changes across conditions, which would show the labels are driven by speaker identity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer-wise Attribution of Explanations to Audio and Frame Tokens
PROPOSAL: Run Qwen2.5-Omni 7B on 1200 MELD and IEMOCAP utterances with sampled explanations over 5 seeds. Derive integrated-gradients attributions from output tokens to the audio and frame tokens at 12 layers, then correlate attribution mass with the modality named in the explanation. Compare attribution profiles for correct and incorrect predictions, and repeat the integration with 3 baseline choices to see whether the modality ranking holds. Report the analysis again on clips where audio and video contradict each other.
CONTROLS: Random-token attribution baseline; attribution to a shuffled audio track; comparison with plain attention weights; a prompt without the clip.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Attribution mass falls mostly on text tokens when explanations cite audio that is absent, and shifts toward frames when a visual cue is genuinely present. It fails if attribution ranking flips across baseline choices, which would make the correlation uninterpretable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Emotion-Specific Preference Tuning with Verified Cue Pairs
PROPOSAL: Construct preference pairs from 8000 MER2024 and MAFW clips: the preferred response lists cues confirmed present by an annotator tag, the rejected one adds an absent cue that commonly co-occurs with the emotion. Tune Qwen2.5-Omni 7B with direct preference optimization using LoRA, then evaluate on a held-out clip set and on an object-level audiovisual hallucination benchmark. Report absent-cue rate, irrelevant-cue rate, and emotion accuracy. Train for 2 epochs at a learning rate of 2e-5 with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Supervised tuning on the preferred responses only; preference tuning with randomly swapped pairs; the base model with a prompt that asks for present cues only; a length-matched control.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Tuned models cut the absent-cue rate relative to supervised tuning at similar accuracy. It fails if swapped pairs give the same gain, showing the effect comes from the training format and not the cue verification.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cue-Verified Supervised Tuning Compared across Backbone Scale
PROPOSAL: Tune Qwen2.5-Omni 3B and 7B on 20000 emotion descriptions whose cue lists were screened against annotator tags, using full fine-tuning for 3 epochs. Evaluate on MER2024 and MAFW held-out clips and on an audiovisual hallucination benchmark. Report absent-cue rate, irrelevant-cue rate and emotion accuracy for each backbone, and fit how the absent-cue reduction depends on the backbone size. Repeat training with 5 seeds for the 7B model to bound variation in the absent-cue rate. Report the gap between backbones per metric, with paired bootstrap intervals over clips.
CONTROLS: Tuning on unscreened descriptions; tuning on label-only targets; base model with a present-cues-only prompt; a data-size matched control.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Screened data cut the absent-cue rate more than unscreened data at both sizes, with the larger gap on the smaller model. It fails if unscreened descriptions work as well, which would mean screening adds little beyond the format.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Contrastive Decoding Against Text-Prior Cues in Audiovisual Emotion Models
PROPOSAL: Implement contrastive decoding for Qwen2.5-Omni 7B in which token logits from the full clip are contrasted with logits from the same prompt with audio and frames removed, down-weighting cues the text prior alone would produce. Sweep the contrast weight over 4 values on a validation split of 500 MAFW clips, then evaluate on 1500 test clips from MAFW and MER2024. Report absent-cue rate, irrelevant-cue rate, emotion accuracy, and description length. Use 3 seeds for sampled decoding and a 2-annotator audit of 200 outputs.
CONTROLS: Greedy decoding; nucleus sampling at 0.9; contrast against a frame-blurred input instead of a removed one; a length penalty alone.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The text-removed contrast lowers absent-cue claims by a clear margin at a small accuracy cost, and blurred-frame contrast helps less. It fails if descriptions become shorter without fewer absent cues per sentence, showing a length effect only.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Visual Contrastive Decoding for Cue Claims on a Reference Subset
PROPOSAL: Apply visual contrastive decoding to Qwen2.5-Omni 7B on 800 MAFW clips, contrasting logits from the clip with logits from a version whose frames are replaced by noise and whose audio is kept. Choose the contrast weight on 300 validation clips from 6 candidate values, then report absent-cue rate, irrelevant-cue rate and emotion accuracy on the remaining clips. Repeat sampling with 8 seeds and measure the agreement of cue claims with 2 annotators on 250 outputs, for greedy decoding and for the contrastive variant.
CONTROLS: Greedy decoding; nucleus sampling at 0.9; contrast against a removed-audio input; a repetition penalty alone.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Contrast against noise frames reduces claims about visual cues that are absent, with little effect on audio cue claims, so the gain is modality-specific. It fails if the audio claims shift as much as the visual ones, which would show the method acts on length and not on priors.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Instruction Tuning Corpus Built from Verified Audiovisual Cue Annotations
PROPOSAL: Assemble an emotion instruction corpus of 30000 clips drawn from MER2024, MAFW, DFEW and MELD. Write cue-grounded responses with a pipeline that proposes cues from an audio tagger and a frame captioner, then keeps only cues present in both annotator tags and tagger outputs. Fine-tune Qwen2.5-Omni 7B with LoRA for 2 epochs on the corpus and on a corpus of the same size with unfiltered cues from a language model. Evaluate absent-cue rate, irrelevant-cue rate and emotion accuracy on held-out clips, with 3 seeds for each corpus.
CONTROLS: Unfiltered corpus of the same size; label-only corpus; tuning on a 5000 clip filtered subset; the base model with few-shot prompting.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The filtered corpus lowers absent-cue claims relative to the unfiltered one at matched accuracy, and the 5000 clip subset recovers most of the gain. It fails if the subset matches the full corpus, since that would show diminishing returns from the extra data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling the Cue-Grounded Instruction Corpus on One Source Domain
PROPOSAL: Use MER2024 only and build cue-grounded emotion responses at 4 corpus sizes from 2000 to 16000 clips, filtered by annotator cue tags. Fine-tune Qwen2.5-Omni 7B with full fine-tuning for 3 epochs at each size, with 3 seeds, and evaluate absent-cue rate, irrelevant-cue rate and emotion accuracy on held-out MER2024 clips and on MAFW clips as an out-of-domain test. Fit a power law to the absent-cue rate against corpus size, report the exponent with a bootstrap interval, and extrapolate to a larger corpus.
CONTROLS: Unfiltered corpus at the same sizes; label-only corpus; base model with few-shot prompting; random subsampling versus difficulty-ordered subsampling.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Absent-cue rate falls smoothly with corpus size and the out-of-domain gain is smaller than the in-domain gain. It fails if the curve flattens after the smallest size, which would show the corpus size is not the limiting factor.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Replication Study of Two-Stage versus Single-Pass Emotion Scoring
PROPOSAL: Compare two ways of scoring emotion descriptions from Qwen2.5-Omni 7B on 500 MER2024 clips: a two-stage pipeline in which an external language model extracts cues and judges them, and a single-pass pipeline using a local classifier trained to flag cue claims absent from annotator tags. Measure agreement between the two with Cohen kappa, and agreement of each with 2 human raters on 300 outputs. Report the variation of the two-stage score across 3 judge prompt wordings and the run-to-run variation of the local classifier over 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Human raters as reference; keyword-match scorer as a floor; the judge with the clip transcript removed; a classifier trained on shuffled labels.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: The local classifier agrees with humans about as well as the two-stage judge and varies less across wordings. It fails if kappa between the two pipelines is low on absent-cue claims, because the benchmark would then depend on the scorer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reproducible Scoring of Emotion Descriptions with Local Classifiers Trained on Cue Tags
PROPOSAL: Train a small encoder classifier on cue claims paired with annotator tags from MAFW and MER2024 to flag claims absent from the clip, then score descriptions from Qwen2.5-Omni 7B and Video-LLaMA2 7B on 1500 clips. Compare classifier agreement with 2 human raters on 600 outputs against a proprietary-judge pipeline, and report variation over training seeds and judge prompt wordings. Release the classifier weights and scoring script with the benchmark. Break results down by emotion category and by clip duration to see whether the scorer is stable for short and long clips.
CONTROLS: Human raters as reference; keyword-match scorer as a floor; the judge without the clip transcript; a classifier trained on shuffled labels.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: The classifier agrees with raters at least as well as the proprietary judge and its scores are more stable over wordings. It fails if agreement drops on long clips, which would limit the classifier as a general scorer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probing Spurious Cue-Emotion Associations with Counterfactual Clips
PROPOSAL: Create counterfactual versions of 300 CREMA-D clips by replacing the face video with a neutral still frame, or by overlaying crying audio on a neutral recording. Ask Qwen2.5-Omni 3B for an emotion label and the cues it relies on. Measure how often the model reports the associated cue that was never edited into the clip, for example tears when only crying audio is present, and how often the label shifts toward the associated emotion. Use 2 prompt wordings and 3 sampling seeds to check stability, and report the shift with bootstrap intervals.
CONTROLS: Unedited clips; edited clips with the claim lexicon applied to reference captions; text-only prompt naming the emotion; a model of a different family on the same clips.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The model reports the associated absent cue in a notable share of edited clips and shifts labels toward the associated emotion. It fails if label shifts appear without cue claims, which would mean the association acts below the explanation level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sentence-Level Cue Co-occurrence Audit of Free-Form Descriptions
PROPOSAL: Collect descriptions from Qwen2.5-Omni 7B on 1000 MELD and MAFW clips over 5 sampling seeds, split them into sentences, and tag each sentence with the cue it asserts using a fixed lexicon. Compute pointwise mutual information between asserted cues and predicted emotions, and compare it with the same statistic from annotator tags to find cue-emotion pairs that the model over-uses. Report the 20 most over-used pairs and test their stability across 2 prompt wordings and 3 decoding temperatures, with confidence intervals from a bootstrap.
CONTROLS: Annotator tags as reference co-occurrence; shuffled emotion labels; the lexicon on reference captions; a model of a different family on the same clips.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Over-used pairs include tears with crying and smiling with laughter, and they persist across wordings. It fails if the over-used pairs are also frequent in annotator tags, in which case the model reflects real co-occurrence and not a prior.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Audiovisual Attention Steering to Counter Text Priors in Emotion Reasoning
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-Omni 7B with an auxiliary loss that raises attention from cue-bearing output tokens to the audio and frame tokens of the clip, using 25000 clips from MER2024, MAFW, DFEW and MELD with annotator cue spans as supervision. Train 3 variants of the loss weight, each with 3 seeds. Evaluate absent-cue rate, irrelevant-cue rate and emotion accuracy on held-out clips and on an audiovisual hallucination benchmark. Examine whether attention mass on the clip rises after training and whether it predicts cue accuracy per output.
CONTROLS: Standard supervised tuning on the same clips; the auxiliary loss with shuffled cue spans; attention steering applied only at inference; the untuned model.
COST: 2500
PREDICTION: Attention to clip tokens rises and absent-cue claims fall compared with standard tuning, with the largest gains at the middle loss weight. It fails if shuffled spans do as well, showing that any attention loss helps, not the grounding signal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Audio-Visual Grounding Loss on a Small Annotated Subset
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune Qwen2.5-Omni 7B on 6000 MER2024 clips with annotator cue spans, adding a loss that aligns the cue-bearing output tokens to the audio and frame tokens they cite. Compare 6 loss weights with 5 seeds each and 3 learning rates, then evaluate on held-out MER2024 clips, MAFW clips and an audiovisual hallucination benchmark. Report absent-cue rate, irrelevant-cue rate and emotion accuracy, and measure whether the attention mass on the clip tokens predicts cue accuracy per output. Save attention maps for a sample of clips to see where the loss moves attention.
CONTROLS: Standard supervised tuning on the same clips; the grounding loss with shuffled cue spans; inference-time attention scaling; the untuned model.
COST: 2500
PREDICTION: The grounding loss lowers absent-cue claims over standard tuning even with the small annotated subset, with weak sensitivity to learning rate. It fails if all loss weights give the same result, which would show the loss is inert.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Cue Perturbation Benchmark Built from Existing Emotion Datasets
PROPOSAL: Construct a benchmark in which 800 clips from MAFW and MER2024 are edited to remove, swap or insert one audio or visual cue, using annotator cue spans to decide what to edit. Evaluate Qwen2.5-Omni 7B, video-SALMONN 2 7B and Video-LLaMA2 7B with multiple-choice questions on whether a named cue is present and which cue explains the emotion. Score with exact match so no external judge enters, and keep the original audio track for visual edits. Report detection accuracy for removed, swapped and inserted cues, and the shift in emotion label, with 3 option orders.
CONTROLS: Unedited clips as a reference; text-only questions; random guessing; a human check of 150 edited clips for edit quality.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Models detect inserted visual cues better than removed audio cues, and label shifts after removal are small. It fails if human checks show many edits are noticeable as artifacts, since detection would then be driven by the edit and not the cue.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Description Faithfulness Study on MELD with Two Backbone Sizes
PROPOSAL: Generate emotion descriptions for 600 MELD clips from Qwen2.5-Omni 3B and 7B at temperature 0.7, with 5 seeds for each model and 2 prompt styles, one asking for cues first and one asking for the emotion first. Decompose descriptions into atomic cue claims with a fixed lexicon and check them against annotator tags from 2 raters. Report the absent-cue rate and the irrelevant-cue rate for each model and prompt style, and plot how the rates depend on the model size and the prompt style with bootstrap intervals.
CONTROLS: Reference captions scored by the same lexicon; clips with audio muted; clips with frames blurred; a random-tag baseline from other clips.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: The larger model has fewer irrelevant cues but similar absent-cue rates, and the cue-first prompt lowers both. It fails if both models give the same rates, in which case size does not affect cue fidelity and the comparison is uninformative.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Decoding-Time Evidence Check for Cue Claims
PROPOSAL: Add a verification step to Qwen2.5-Omni 7B in which each generated cue claim is turned into a yes-or-no question about the clip and answered by the same model with the clip present, dropping claims answered no. Test on 700 MAFW clips and 700 MER2024 clips, and report absent-cue rate, irrelevant-cue rate, recall of annotator cues and emotion accuracy before and after verification. Run 3 seeds for sampled outputs and a 200 output audit by 2 annotators of the verifier's decisions.
CONTROLS: No verification; verification with the clip removed; verification by a smaller model; random dropping of claims at the same rate.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Verification removes a large share of absent cues at a modest loss of recall, and clip-removed verification removes none selectively. It fails if the verifier agrees with its own generated claims regardless of the clip, which the clip-removed run would reveal.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Retraining-Free Cue Filtering with Large Reference Model Votes
PROPOSAL: Filter cue claims from Qwen2.5-Omni 7B on 1500 MAFW and MER2024 clips by asking 3 other audiovisual models and 2 larger models whether each claim is supported by the clip, keeping claims supported by a majority. Report absent-cue rate, irrelevant-cue rate, recall of annotator cues and emotion accuracy before and after filtering, and measure agreement between the voters with Fleiss kappa. Run with 5 seeds for sampled outputs and check 250 outputs with 2 annotators. Compare voter agreement for the greedy outputs and for the sampled outputs.
CONTROLS: No filtering; filtering with the clip removed; filtering with a single voter; random dropping of claims at the same rate.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Majority filtering removes most absent cues at modest recall loss, and larger voters agree with annotators more than smaller ones. It fails if voters share the same errors, so that kappa is high but annotator agreement does not rise.
